newsitem.title: UK: Gibraltar governor reassures on sovereignty.
newsitem.headline: Gibraltar governor reassures on sovereignty.

text.p: The governor of Gibraltar told the colony's citizens on Monday that they need not fear any weakening of Britain's commitment towards them.

Sir Richard Luce, a former British Foreign Office minister, acknowledged there was "some anxiety" in Gibraltar because he was the first civilian governor to be appointed since Britain acquired the colony nearly 300 years ago. All his predecessors have been military men.

In a speech to Gibraltar's House of Assembly, Luce said his appointment last December to the largely ceremonial post signified "no change whatsoever" in Britain's commitment to the colony and there was "no hidden agenda".
Britain would not allow any loss of sovereignty against the will of the people of Gibraltar, he said.
"This is a fundamental safeguard for the people of Gibraltar, the importance of which no-one in Gibraltar should underestimate.
"For this reason I need make no apology for reiterating this vital commitment," Luce said in his speech, the text of which was released in London.
Last month Spain proposed sharing sovereignty over Gibraltar for the next 100 years with control of the colony then passing to Madrid. Britain rejected the proposal.
Gibraltar, adamant that it does not want to become Spanish, has had to shift its economic centre of gravity since Britain's military presence on the rock has declined.
The Navy dockyard closed in 1984 and the regular British Army battalion stationed on the colony was withdrawn in 1991.
Luce welcomed a clampdown on drug and tobacco smuggling and money laundering, saying the latter in particular posed a threat to Gibraltar's financial services sector.
